Implement GitHub issue #83 in AlexITC/expense-tracker: improve the expense dedup flow to detect orphaned row-less duplicates and add bulk dedup with per-row checkboxes. Full spec follows.

## Problem

The expense dedup flow only handles one shape of duplicate: a row-linked expense (survivor) paired with a receipt-bearing, row-less expense (loser). See `web/.../utils/ExpenseDuplicateDetector.scala` (survivor = `rowIds.nonEmpty && receiptIds.isEmpty`, loser = `rowIds.isEmpty` and has a receipt).

This misses a second, common shape: **orphaned duplicates left after deleting a duplicate bank statement.** When the same statement was imported twice and one copy is deleted, that copy's expenses lose their row and become row-less with **no receipt**. Each one duplicates a surviving row-linked expense (same amount, same date, same merchant), but because the orphan has no receipt it is neither a survivor nor a loser under the current rules, so the UI never surfaces it. A real cleanup produced dozens of such orphans and the UI flagged none of them.

## Goal

1. **Detect orphan duplicates.** Extend the detector to also pair a row-linked survivor with a row-less, receipt-less twin (same amount, date within the existing window, merchant for the Strong tier). For this shape the orphan carries nothing to fold in, so the "merge" degenerates to deleting the orphan; the surviving row-linked expense already holds the real data (splits stay with it).

2. **Bulk dedup.** Add a checkbox on each duplicate candidate row plus a bulk action button, so a large batch (the orphan case produces many at once) can be processed in one go instead of one dialog at a time. Selecting rows and clicking the bulk button resolves all selected candidates. Keep the per-candidate action too.

## Notes

- Preserve the existing receipt-vs-row behavior unchanged; this adds a case, it does not replace one.
- Keep the ambiguity handling: when an expense appears in more than one candidate, it still needs review, so a bulk run must not silently resolve ambiguous candidates without the user picking the right partner. Decide how bulk interacts with ambiguous pairs (e.g. bulk applies only to unambiguous Strong candidates; ambiguous ones stay manual).
- The two merge shapes differ: receipt-vs-row moves a receipt onto the survivor; orphan-vs-row just deletes the orphan. The bulk path must do the right one per candidate.
- All user-owned queries scoped by `user_id`.
